source: JoSAA 2025 Round 6 official ORCR archive (IIITs; cross-checked against a collegedunia PDF mirror), JAC Delhi/IIITD official 2025 Round 5 document, IIITB official 2025 cut-offs, IIITH via careers360/getmyuni mirrors, BITS official final BITSAT 2025 cut-offs; BITS->JEE Main mapping estimated (see bitsat_to_main)

bitsat_to_main.reasoning: Step 1 - BITSAT score -> BITSAT merit position. BITS no longer publishes ranks, but it did publish an official BITSAT-2022 score distribution (390 scale): number of candidates scoring >=351: 216, >=329: 675, >=307: 1414, >=285: 2580, >=263: 4633, >=241: 7669, >=219: 11845, >=197: 17373, >=184: 21364, >=175: 24366. Log-linear interpolation of that table gives each programme's 2022 closing merit position from its official 2022 cut-off. The 2025 paper was harder (cut-offs fell 16-33 marks at the top vs 2024 and the score scale compressed), so 2025 scores cannot be read off the 2022 table directly. Instead, assuming each programme's merit position is roughly stable year to year, I regressed ln(2022 merit position) on the 2025 cut-off across all 36 B.E./M.Sc. programmes offered in both years: ln(r) = 16.945 - 0.03265*score (R^2 = 0.983, residual SD 0.12). Each 10 BITSAT-2025 marks is about a 1.39x change in merit position. Pilani CSE (304) maps to about 1,100; Goa CSE (274) about 3,000; Pilani Civil (206) about 27,000. Step 2 - BITSAT merit position -> JEE Main CRL rank. The BITSAT pool is a subset of the JEE Main pool, so the same ability sits at a larger JEE Main rank. The multiplier k comes from three pieces of evidence: (a) peer-choice commentary puts Pilani CSE alongside NIT Trichy/NITK CSE, which closed at OS ranks 1,449/1,827 in JoSAA 2025 (k about 1.3-1.6; preference overstates difficulty because BITS draws students who would rank lower in JEE); (b) CollegeDekho states the Pilani CSE cut-off is about a 4k JEE Main rank (k about 3.6); (c) a self-reported 2022 data point, BITSAT 324/390 with JEE Main 99.442 percentile (about CRL 5,000 of about 9.05 lakh candidates), at a 2022 BITSAT position of about 800 (k about 6.3, inflated by regression to the mean). Their geometric mean is about 3.2, so I use k = 3: main_equiv = 3 * exp(16.945 - 0.03265*score), rounded. JoSAA OPEN/OS closing ranks for 36 NIT CSE/ECE/EEE programmes moved only slightly from 2022 to 2025 (median ratio 1.06), so no year adjustment is applied. Uncertainty: k could plausibly be anywhere from 1.5 to 6, so treat each main_equiv as within about 2x either way. Each entry's note gives its range. The ordering among BITS programmes is more reliable than the absolute level. Known biases: BITS added seats after 2022 (MnC, Electronics & Computer, Environmental), which pushes true 2025 positions slightly deeper; and a constant k ignores that BITSAT participation may differ at different rank levels.
